arxiv-1709-00233.title: A new kind of uniqueness theorems for inverse Sturm-Liouville problems
arxiv-1709-00233.creator: Yuri Ashrafyan
arxiv-1709-00233.description: Abstract We prove Marchenko-type uniqueness theorems for inverse Sturm-Liouville problems. Moreover, we prove a generalization of Ambarzumyan theorem. Keywords: Inverse problem, Sturm-Liouville operator, uniqueness theorem, Ambarzumyan theorem 1 Introduction Let us denote by L(q,\alpha,\beta) the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem \displaystyle-y^{\prime\prime}+q(x)y=\mu y,\quad x\in(0,\pi),\ \mu\in\mathbb{C}, (1.1) \displaystyle y(0)\cot\alpha+y^{\prime}(0)=0,\qquad\alpha\in(0,\pi), (1.2) \displaystyle y(\pi)\cot\beta+y^{\prime}(\pi)=0,\qquad\beta\in(0,\pi), (1.3) where q is a real-valued, summable function, q\in L^{1}_{\mathbb{R}}(0,\pi) .

arxiv-2102-06796.title: An accreting stellar binary model for active periodic fast radio bursts
arxiv-2102-06796.creator: Can-Min Deng, Shu-Qing Zhong, Zi-Gao Dai
arxiv-2102-06796.description: Abstract In this work, we propose an accreting stellar binary model for understanding the active periodic fast radio bursts (FRBs). The system consists of a stellar compact object (CO) and a donor star (DS) companion in an eccentric orbit, where the DS fills its own Roche lobe near the periastron.

arxiv-2103-04135.title: Hard gluon evolution in warming medium
arxiv-2103-04135.creator: F. G. Ben, M. V. T. Machado
arxiv-2103-04135.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by F. G. Ben, M. V. T. Machado. We describe the energy distribution of hard gluons travelling through a dense quark-gluon plasma whose temperature increases linearly with time, within a probabilistic perturbative approach. The results were applied to the thermalization problem in heavy ion collisions.

arxiv-2210-03340.title: A Novel Graph-based Motion Planner of Multi-Mobile Robot Systems with Formation and Obstacle Constraints
arxiv-2210-03340.creator: Wenhang Liu, Jiawei Hu, Heng Zhang, Michael Yu Wang, Zhenhua Xiong
arxiv-2210-03340.description: Abstract Multi-mobile robot systems show great advantages over one single robot in many applications. However, the robots are required to form desired task-specified formations, making feasible motions decrease significantly. Thus, it is challenging to determine whether the robots can pass through an obstructed environment under formation constraints, especially in an obstacle-rich environment.

arxiv-2303-01497.title: Teach a Robot to FISH: Versatile Imitation from One Minute of Demonstrations
arxiv-2303-01497.creator: Siddhant Haldar*, Jyothish Pari*, Anant Rai, Lerrel Pinto
arxiv-2303-01497.description: Abstract While imitation learning provides us with an efficient toolkit to train robots, learning skills that are robust to environment variations remains a significant challenge. Current approaches address this challenge by relying either on large amounts of demonstrations that span environment variations or on handcrafted reward functions that require state estimates. Both directions are not scalable to fast imitation.

arxiv-2304-04981.title: Contingent Fees in Order Flow Auctions Thanks: Resnick gratefully acknowledges support from a Flashbots grant which funded this work. Comments from Quintus Kilbourn and Mallesh Pai were greatly appreciated
arxiv-2304-04981.creator: Max Resnick A {}^{\text{A}}
arxiv-2304-04981.description: Abstract . Many early order flow auction designs handle the payment for orders when they execute on the chain rather than when they are won in the auction. Payments in these auctions only take place when the orders are executed, creating a free option for whoever wins the order.

arxiv-2408-12365.title: Enhancing Uncertainty Communication in Time Series Predictions: Insights and Recommendations
arxiv-2408-12365.creator: A. Karagappa 1 , P. Kaur Betz 1 , J. Gilg 1 , M. Zeumer 1 , A. Gerndt 1 and B. Preim 2 1 Institute for Software Technology, DLR, Braunschweig, Germany 2 Faculty of Computer Science, University of Magdeburg, Magdeburg, Germany
arxiv-2408-12365.description: Abstract As the world increasingly relies on mathematical models for forecasts in different areas, effective communication of uncertainty in time series predictions is important for informed decision making. This study explores how users estimate probabilistic uncertainty in time series predictions under different variants of line charts depicting uncertainty.

arxiv-2504-13073.title: Topological defect engineering enables size and shape control in self-assembly
arxiv-2504-13073.creator: Lara Koehler, Markus Eder, Christoph Karfusehr, Vincent Ouazan-Reboul, Pierre Ronceray, Friedrich C. Simmel, Martin Lenz
arxiv-2504-13073.description: Abstract The self-assembly of complex structures from engineered subunits is a major goal of nanotechnology, but controlling their size becomes increasingly difficult in larger assemblies. Existing strategies present significant challenges, among which are the use of multiple subunit types or the precise control of their shape and mechanics.

arxiv-2505-16053.title: Learning from Algorithm Feedback: One-Shot Sat Solver Guidance with GNNs
arxiv-2505-16053.creator: Jan Tönshoff, Martin Grohe
arxiv-2505-16053.description: Abstract Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) solvers are foundational to computer science, yet their performance typically hinges on hand-crafted heuristics. This work introduces Reinforcement Learning from Algorithm Feedback (RLAF) as a paradigm for learning to guide SAT solver branching heuristics with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).

arxiv-2510-20865.title: Philip Warren Anderson 13 December, 1923 - 20 March 2020 Elected FRS 1980
arxiv-2510-20865.creator: Premala Chandra, Piers Coleman, Clare C. Yu, [6pt] Department of Physics, Royal Holloway, University of London, Egham, Surrey TW20 0EX, UK., [6pt] Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of California, Irvine, Irvine, CA 92697, USA [6pt]
arxiv-2510-20865.description: Abstract Philip Warren Anderson was a pioneering theoretical physicist whose work fundamentally shaped our understanding of complex systems. Anderson received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1977 for his groundbreaking research on localization and magnetism, yet he did so much more. His work on magnetism included antiferromagnetism, superexchange, the Kondo problem and local magnetic moments in metals.

pmc-11324355.title: Training in Public Health Informatics and Technology Leveraging a Multi-institutional Partnership Model and Emphasizing Experiential Learning
pmc-11324355.creator: Sripriya Rajamani, Kristie C. Waterfield, Robin Austin, Vivian Singletary, Yasmin Odowa, Stephanie Miles-Richardson, Tony Winters, Brenton Powers, Feather LaRoche, Sarah Trachet, Jennifer Fritz, Jonathon P. Leider, Rebecca Wurtz, Gulzar H. Shah
pmc-11324355.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and Objective Though public health is an information-intense profession, there is a paucity of workforce with Public Health Informatics and Technology (PHIT) skills, which was evident during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. This need is addressed through the PHIT workforce program (2021–2025) by the Office of the National Coordinator for training and to increase racial and ethnic diversity in the PHIT workforce.

pmc-11382315.title: Bioactive components in prunella vulgaris for treating Hashimoto's disease via regulation of innate immune response in human thyrocytes
pmc-11382315.creator: Yongzhao Chen, Bo Jiang, Cheng Qu, Chaoyu Jiang, Chen Zhang, Yanxue Wang, Fei Chen, Xitai Sun, Lei Su, Yuqian Luo
pmc-11382315.description: BackgroundHashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) is a thyroid autoimmune disease characterized by lymphocytic infiltration and thyroid destruction. Prunella vulgaris (PV) is a traditional Chinese herbal medicine with documented clinical efficacy in treating HT. We previously reported an immunoregulatory effect of PV in thyrocytes; however, the bioactive components of PV remained unclear.

pmc-11583048.title: General anaesthesia and deep sedation for monopolar pulsed field ablation using a lattice-tip catheter combined with a novel three-dimensional mapping system
pmc-11583048.creator: Andreas Rillig, Jun Hirokami, Fabian Moser, Stefano Bordignon, Laura Rottner, Tohoku Shota, Ilaria My, Andrea Urbani, Marc Lemoine, Joseph Kheir, Niklas Schenker, Lukas Urbanek, Katarina Govorov, David Schaack, Julius Obergassel, Jan Riess, Djemail Ismaili, Paulus Kirchhof, Feifan Ouyang, Boris Schm
pmc-11583048.description: AimsA novel three-dimensional mapping platform combined with a lattice-tip catheter that can toggle between monopolar pulsed field ablation (PFA) and radiofrequency energy delivery was recently launched. So far, the system was predominantly applied in general anaesthesia (GA), not in deep sedation.

pmc-11712813.title: The role of biofluid markers in predicting near‐term cognitive impairment
pmc-11712813.creator: Yara Yakoub, Fernando Gonzalez‐Ortiz, Nicholas J. Ashton, Thomas K Karikari, Cherie Strikwerda‐Brown, Frédéric St‐Onge, Valentin Ourry, Michael Schöll, Maiya R. Geddes, Simon Ducharme, Pedro Rosa‐Neto, Jean‐Paul Soucy, John C.S. Breitner, Henrik Zetterberg, Kaj Blennow, Judes Poirier, Sylvia Villene
pmc-11712813.description: BackgroundPET biomarkers have proven valuable for identifying cognitively unimpaired (CU) individuals at‐risk of near‐term clinical progression. Given the increasing interest in plasma biomarkers to detect Alzheimer’s pathology, we assessed levels of amyloid (Aß42/40) and tau (p‐tau217 and p‐tau181) biomarkers in plasma (A+T+plasma) in CU individuals as predictors of clinical progression to mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

pmc-12594465.title: Case Report of a Dermatologic Reaction to Wound Closure Strips and Liquid Adhesive
pmc-12594465.creator: Amal Asghar, Trevor Smith, Matthew Underwood, Tommy Y Kim
pmc-12594465.description: Type IV hypersensitivity reactions are delayed, cell-mediated reactions between T cells and antigens that normally occur usually within 48 to 72 hours after exposure to an antigen. This is a case of a 51-year-old male status post left Achilles tendon repair with findings consistent with a type IV hypersensitivity reaction on post-operative day 12.

pmc-12658187.title: EZH2 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma and its relationship with circadian rhythm-related genes
pmc-12658187.creator: Xingyue Wang, Miaolong He, Limian Zhou, Wei Chen
pmc-12658187.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most prevalent liver malignancy, with increasing incidence and high mortality, primarily associated with hepatitis virus infection and cirrhosis. Herein, we explored the association between enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2) expression and HCC progression, prognosis, and circadian rhythm-related genes.

pmc-12785195.title: Development of production methodologies for scFv-Fc conjugated critical reagents to support CAR-T clinical programs
pmc-12785195.creator: Ellen O’Connor, Eric Lachacz, Jared Delmar, Bradley D’souza, Samuel Edwards, Christopher Griffin, Rosie Lin, Neil Mody, Alicia Salas, Natalia Schoch-Lopez, Mitali Shah, Ai Shih, Dewald van Dyk, Yueming Xu
pmc-12785195.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionRoutine conjugation protocols are typically used by bioanalytical laboratories for production of their assay critical reagents. Novel molecules can pose unique challenges to the production of high-quality conjugated critical reagents required for clinical bioanalytical assays.

pmc-13443540.title: Etiology-guided mutational signature learning from DNA repair knockouts in cell lines using supervised NMF
pmc-13443540.creator: Sander Goossens, Yasin I Tepeli, Colm Seale, Joana P Gonçalves
pmc-13443540.description: Many tumours show deficiencies in DNA damage response (DDR), not only driving tumorigenesis but also exposing vulnerabilities with therapeutic potential. Assessing which patients might benefit from DDR-targeting therapy requires knowledge of tumour DDR deficiency (DDRd) status, with mutational signatures reportedly better predictors than loss-of-function mutations. Existing DDRd models offer effective prediction for pathways with well-characterized processes and mutational signatures.

pmc-13628185.title: Disentangling visually driven tactile predictions from multisensory integration in body ownership
pmc-13628185.creator: Renzo C Lanfranco, Marie Chancel, Birgit Hasenack, H Henrik Ehrsson
pmc-13628185.description: The sense of owning one’s body is essential for distinguishing internal from external sensations. Research using bodily illusions shows that this sense depends on integrating visual, tactile and proprioceptive signals, yet the role of multisensory predictions remains unclear. We addressed this using a modified rubber hand illusion.

pmc-13633664.title: How reliable is the use of ovarian dilatations for mosquito age-grading? A blinded multi-rater validation of the Polovodova method in Anopheles mosquitoes
pmc-13633664.creator: Doreen Josen Siria, Halfan Ngowo, Emmanuel Hape, Mohamed Jumanne, Gerald Tamayamali, Laurent Mtima, Heather M Ferguson, Fredros Okumu, Francesco Baldini, Julian Hillyer
pmc-13633664.description: Accurate estimation of mosquito age is critical for malaria surveillance, as only older female Anopheles mosquitoes can transmit the parasite. Traditional age-grading methods include the Polovodova technique in which dilatations on the ovarian pedicel to tally completed gonotrophic cycles (GC) are counted.
